psych-soc-01-c1.text: Rose M. Spielman, William J. Jenkins, Marilyn D. Lovett (OpenStax) (2020). Psychology 2e, section 12.4 Conformity, Compliance, and Obedience. OpenStax, Rice University.
psych-soc-01-c1.quote: Asch (1955) found that 76% of participants conformed to group pressure at least once by indicating the incorrect line.
psych-soc-01-c1.claim: About 75% of participants conformed at least once

psych-soc-01-c2.text: Stanley Milgram (1963). Behavioral Study of Obedience. Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology 67(4), 371-378.
psych-soc-01-c2.quote: Of the 40 subjects, 26 obeyed the orders of the experimenter to the end, proceeding to punish the victim until they reached the most potent shock available on the shock generator.
psych-soc-01-c2.claim: In fact, about 65% of participants delivered the full 450-volt shock

psych-soc-01-c3.text: Cecilia L. Ridgeway. Compliance and Conformity. Encyclopedia of Sociology (Gale), via Encyclopedia.com.
psych-soc-01-c3.quote: Morton Deutsch and Harold Gerard (1955) labelled these informational influence and normative influence.
psych-soc-01-c3.claim: In 1955 Deutsch and Gerard drew a now-standard distinction between two reasons we conform.
